summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT egress gateway for node2 and node3 on the private "lan" network (eth1, 10.50.50.0/24), implemented entirely via Ansible run from node4 (the designated control_node). node2/node3 got static LAN IPs with a default route via node1 preferred (lower metric) over the mgmt network. node1 got a static LAN address, a masquerade NAT source rule (10.50.50.0/24 -> eth0), and a forward-filter default-accept, with ip_forward already enabled. Verified end-to-end that node2/node3 reach the internet only via node1 (disabled the NAT rule, observed loss, restored it, observed recovery). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; each showed a changed OS boot_id and full recovery of its role (NAT/interface state on node1, static IP/route/egress on node2 and node3, working Ansible control and a clean idempotent playbook re-run on node4), with node2/node3 internet reachability reconfirmed after all four restarts.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: mgmt network (eth0, dhcp+egress) shared by all 4 nodes, and a private lan network (eth1, no dhcp, no egress) shared by node1-3; node4 is the Ansible control_node with only mgmt
Established passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (VyOS 'vyos' user via system login public-keys config), node2 and node3 (root authorized_keys)

Playbook: community.general.nmcli static IP + preferred default route (metric 50) on node2/node3 eth1; VyOS configure/set/commit/save NAT masquerade rule + LAN interface address + forward-filter default-accept on node1
Diagnosed and fixed a VyOS shell alias-expansion bug where 'set -e' silently broke the configure/commit/exit alias chain when run non-interactively via ansible.builtin.shell
Ran the playbook via node4's run.sh entrypoint twice, confirming idempotency (second run reported no changes)
Verified egress (ping/curl from node2 and node3 to 1.1.1.1 through node1) and proved dependency on node1 by disabling then re-enabling the NAT source rule
Captured boot_id baselines on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polling exec availability and confirming changed boot_id for each

After each restart, re-verified the node's required state: node1's NAT rule/eth1 address/ip_forward, node2/node3's static IP/route/egress ping, and node4's ability to re-run the Ansible playbook idempotently against the whole cluster
Final full-cluster ping check from node2 and node3 to 1.1.1.1 confirmed persistent NAT egress after all restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as NAT gateway for node2/node3 (masquerade rule, LAN address, forwarding)
evidence.summary: VyOS configure/commit/save applied interface eth1 10.50.50.254/24, NAT source rule 100 masquerading 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0, forward-filter default-accept; ip_forward=1 confirmed; ansible run shows the rule active and idempotent

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 reach the internet through node1 (implemented via Ansible)
evidence.summary: Ansible ad-hoc ping confirmed inventory reachability; nat-egress.yml run from node4 set static LAN IPs and preferred routes; node2/node3 route to 1.1.1.1 goes via eth1/node1 and ping+curl succeed (ttl=56, one hop via node1)

evidence.requirement: Dependency on node1's NAT proven (smallest safe disruption)
evidence.summary: Disabling NAT source rule 100 on node1 caused immediate ping loss from node2; re-enabling and saving the rule restored connectivity for both node2 and node3
inventory.ini and nat-egress.yml built on node4 (control_node); run.sh execution shows all tasks 'ok' with changed=0 on the settled run, confirming idempotency

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9028a473...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during restart; post-restart boot_id changed to 5a47750d...; NAT rule, eth1 address, ip_forward, and node2/node3 ping through node1 all recovered

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9bdcc129...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to e80a61f6...; static eth1 IP, preferred default route via node1, and successful ping to 1.1.1.1 all recovered

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 84419b90...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to f4e1185b...; static eth1 IP, preferred default route, and ping to 1.1.1.1 all recovered

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to a4ad4787...; Ansible control files intact and nat-egress.yml re-ran idempotently against node1-3, with node2/node3 internet ping reconfirmed
